description: Experience the iconic taste of San Francisco with this authentic sourdough boule recipe, featuring its signature tangy flavor and wonderfully chewy texture. This bread boasts a crisp, golden crust and an airy, open crumb, perfect for any meal. Mastering this classic American bake will bring the aroma and taste of a true artisanal bakery right into your kitchen.

instructions.title: Prepare the Levain and Autolyse
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine the active sourdough starter with warm water and mix until the starter is mostly dissolved. Add the bread flour and whole wheat flour, mixing by hand until no dry bits remain. Cover the bowl and let it rest for 30-60 minutes. This process, called autolyse, helps the flour hydrate and gluten develop.

instructions.title: Incorporate Salt and First Knead
instructions.text: After the autolyse, add the fine sea salt to the dough. Wet your hands slightly and gently fold and squeeze the dough for about 5 minutes to fully incorporate the salt and begin strengthening the gluten. The dough will become more cohesive. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Perform Stretch and Folds
instructions.text: Over the next 2-3 hours, perform 3-4 sets of stretch and folds every 30-45 minutes. To do this, gently stretch a portion of the dough up and fold it over itself, rotating the bowl a quarter turn and repeating until all sides are folded. This builds strength and elasticity in the dough. Cover the bowl between sets.

instructions.title: Bulk Fermentation and Pre-Shaping
instructions.text: After the stretch and folds, let the dough bulk ferment at room temperature (70-75F) until it has increased in volume by about 20-30% and feels airy. This can take 2-4 hours depending on your starter's activity and room temperature. Gently turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and pre-shape it into a round. Let it rest for 20 minutes.

instructions.title: Final Shaping and Cold Proof
instructions.text: Lightly flour your hands and the dough. Gently shape the dough into a tight boule, creating surface tension. Place the shaped dough seam-side up into a floured banneton or a bowl lined with a floured cloth. Cover tightly with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 12-18 hours for the cold proof. This develops flavor and makes the dough easier to handle.

instructions.title: Baking the Boule
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 500F (260C) with a Dutch oven inside for at least 45 minutes. Carefully remove the hot Dutch oven, invert the cold dough into it, score the top with a sharp blade, and spritz with a little water. Cover and bake for 20 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 450F (230C), remove the lid, and bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until the crust is deep golden brown.

instructions.title: Cooling
instructions.text: Once baked, carefully remove the boule from the Dutch oven and transfer it to a wire rack to cool completely for at least 1-2 hours before slicing. This allows the internal structure to set and improves the flavor and texture.

tips: For that authentic San Francisco tang, ensure your starter is very active and has been fed regularly. A longer cold proof also enhances the sour flavor.
Using a mix of bread flour and a small amount of whole wheat flour gives the boule a better texture and deeper flavor. You can adjust the whole wheat percentage to your liking.
Always allow your sourdough to cool completely on a wire rack before slicing. Cutting into it too soon can result in a gummy texture and collapse the internal structure.
